rows.description: A child looking at a night sky or a huge river feels small yet strangely happy. Awe expands the sense of the world and, oddly, softens self-focus.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: joy, affection, awe

rows.description: A teenager moved by a scientist, a mountain, a devotional song or a stranger's kindness feels lifted beyond daily worries. Awe can arise from moral beauty as much as from scenery.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 23–26
related mind states: anger, anxiety, awe

rows.description: A young adult makes time for a pilgrimage, a trek, a concert or an observatory night. Deliberate awe reduces petty stress and reminds a person that their problems are part of something larger.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17
related mind states: awe

rows.description: Someone standing with a friend before a great view sees the friend go quiet and does not fill the silence with talk. Letting awe breathe is a quiet kindness.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17
related mind states: awe, relief from stress

rows.description: A child rests quietly in a parent's lap and breathes slowly. Early serenity is borrowed from a calm adult, and the child stores it as a felt memory of safety.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: calm, trust, relief from stress

rows.description: A child learns to slow breathing, drink water or step outside after being upset. Calming skills taught before the storm work far better than those demanded during it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: calm, relief from stress

rows.description: Peers see a composed teenager and assume they do not care. Real serenity notices the problem fully and chooses not to be thrown, which differs from indifference.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: calm

rows.description: A student before an interview or a viva feels nerves yet stays steady, having accepted that not everything is in their control. Calm here is a practised stance, not the absence of fear.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: fear, calm

rows.description: A worried person feels their own panic ease near a calm friend or elder. Calm spreads between people, and being that steadiness for another is a real gift.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: anxiety, calm

rows.description: A child says thank you because they were told to, without yet feeling it. Repetition and modelling by adults plant the habit long before the feeling arrives.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: gratitude
